chapters.title: Sales Performance
facts: ₹32,06,431 of cash from 272 transactions and 179 buyers in September 2026, at an average of ₹17,913 each.
59% of that cash has already been delivered as attended classes (₹19,01,973).
53 buyers (30%) bought more than once and produced 38% of the month.
chapters.subtitle: ₹32,06,431 of cash, 179 buyers, ₹17,913 each
recs_extra: Re-price the ladder so the bigger commitment is always cheaper per class
Sales + Finance
4 Class Package sells at ₹12,403 a class while Private Class sells at ₹60,296; 14 lines went out at the dearer per-class rate.

Moving even a quarter of the 21 class-count sales onto the best per-class tier adds credits to the delivered base at no revenue cost, and removes the single clearest pricing inconsistency on the board.
Sell the second purchase while the first is being served
Front Desk
53 of 179 buyers bought more than once and produced 38% of the cash. 70% bought once and were not offered anything further.

A renewal conversation at the moment of highest engagement is worth more than the same conversation in an email three weeks later; on this month’s mix it is the difference between a one-purchase member and a repeat one.
Put every discount code under one owner and one ceiling
Marketing + Finance
9 codes were used in September 2026, giving away ₹12,65,715 at depths between 10% and 70%. The largest single code is 79% of all discounting.
One owner and one depth cap turns discounting from a leak into a lever, and makes the month comparable to next month.
Lead with 3 Month Unlimited, not with the cheapest offer
Sales + Marketing
Lifetime value by first purchase ranges from ₹14,793 (Session) to ₹1,17,275 (3 Month Unlimited) across 949 recorded first-timers.
The first product decides the lifetime. Changing which offer the desk leads with costs nothing and moves the whole cohort.
Own the interval between the first visit and the second
Front Desk + Studio Manager
Members who came back within a day of a first visit are worth ₹38,956 across a lifetime; those who took over a month are worth ₹26,543.
Booking the next class before the member leaves the building converts the only moment when they are certain they want to come back.

The largest category was Memberships at ₹16,30,524. Class revenue reached ₹19,01,973 at ₹5,799 a class.

Put a named owner on the largest category
Sales + Studio Manager
Memberships produced ₹16,30,524 of the month’s ₹32,06,431 across 33 transactions.
The largest line in any month deserves a target, a price test and a person accountable for it. Managing the total hides the composition.
Sell the next purchase at the point of the last one
Front Desk
The average buyer spent ₹17,913 and repeat buying at this studio clusters tightly around a monthly rhythm.
A renewal offered while a member is at peak usage converts far more often than one offered after the visits have already stopped.
Report cash per buyer, not just cash
Finance
Revenue per class is ₹5,799 and revenue per attendance ₹910; the buyer, not the seat, is the unit that has to be replaced.
A studio can grow transactions while shrinking buyers. One column prevents that.
Staff the desk where the money already is
Front Desk + Studio Manager
The busiest trading hour of the month was 10:00, taking 45 transactions.
Placing the sales conversation in that hour costs nothing and works with the members’ own routine rather than against it.
Watch the discount mix, not the discount total
Marketing + Finance
15% of sales carried a discount at 28.3% depth, against 10% at 6.4% a year earlier.
Depth and spread move independently, and only one of them is visible in the revenue line.
Put a second pair of hands on the counter at the peak hour
Front Desk
10:00 took 45 transactions, 00:00 took 1.
The counter is the only place where a faster response converts directly into a larger ticket. Staffing should follow the hour grid, not the shift rota.
Give the top two categories a bundle price
Sales + Marketing
Memberships and Class Packages together produced ₹22,77,168, 71% of the month, across 74 transactions.
Two categories that are usually bought together can be priced together. It raises the average ticket without touching list prices.
Cap the depth and keep the spread
Finance + Management
15% of transactions carried a discount at 19.3% average depth, on ₹61,83,821 of gross value.
Spread is a policy decision and depth is a margin decision. Publishing an approved depth band converts an open negotiation into a rule the desk can apply.
Set a daily transaction target, not just a monthly one
Studio Manager
272 transactions across the month is 9.1 a day, against 179 buyers.
A daily number is visible while the month can still be changed. Monthly totals only ever arrive as news.

chapters.title: Class Performance
facts: 328 classes, 4,606 seats, 2,090 attendances and 45.4% utilisation in September 2026.
₹19,01,973 of class revenue at ₹5,799 a class and ₹910 per attendance.
235 booked seats went empty; 234 of those were late cancellations.
chapters.subtitle: 328 classes at 45.4% utilisation, ₹5,799 a class
recs_extra: Recover the 61 booked seats PowerCycle leaves empty
Studio Manager + Programming
PowerCycle is the largest single source of unoccupied booked seats this month: 61 of them, on a 87% show rate against a studio-wide 90%.

The scale of the format is what makes the number worth chasing: one class a week tighter, or a waitlist that fires the moment a seat returns, recovers roughly 15 seats a month without a single new member being asked for money.
Review every class that ran to nobody before it is scheduled again
Programming
4 classes in September 2026 were taught to an empty room, concentrated in PowerCycle (3).
Each one is a paid hour that produced nothing. A monthly rule - three empties and the slot is retired or re-timed - is the cheapest capacity the studio has.
Close or re-time the hour nobody uses
Programming + Studio Manager
10:00 fills at 50% while 16:00 fills at 28% on 10 classes.
Moving an hour of capacity from the weakest slot to the strongest is a same-month change to utilisation that needs no new members, no price change and no marketing spend.
Set a minimum viable class size and publish it
Programming
35 classes ran to one or two people out of 328. A room of two costs the same as a room of ten and reads, to the member in it, as a class nobody wants.
Merging thin classes into the adjacent slot protects the format and raises the perceived quality of both.
Give event classes a purpose and a number
Marketing + Studio Manager
5 hosted or partner sessions took 60 attendances (3%) and ₹0 of revenue on 2% of the month\’s capacity.
Decide in advance whether each event is buying reach or making money, and the next month can be judged on the one that was chosen.

Cut or re-time the sessions nobody comes to
Programming + Studio Manager
39 classes ran to two people or fewer and 4 had nobody at all.
Every empty class costs the same as a full one. Moving those hours is a timetable edit and it is reversible after four weeks.
Rebuild the weakest hour of the day
Programming
16:00 was the emptiest hour of the month at 28% utilisation across 10 classes.
One hour, repeated weekly, is the cheapest capacity decision available. It should be a test with a review date, not a habit.
Match the room to the demand, not the format
Studio Manager
10 to 11 seats filled 59.4% while 14 or more seats filled 39.6%.
Small rooms fill and large ones do not. Where the timetable allows, the smaller room for the same class raises utilisation with no new demand.
Publish utilisation weekly, by day and hour
Studio Manager
The month’s utilisation was 45.4% against 43.3% a year earlier.
A weekly number turns a monthly post-mortem into a decision the team can still act on.
Rebuild the weakest weekday before adding any class
Programming + Studio Manager
Friday filled 39.2% across 37 classes while Tuesday filled 49.3%.
Shifting a class from the weakest day to the strongest costs nothing and lifts the room without touching the timetable size.
Test a smaller room in the emptiest hours
Studio Manager
16:00 ran 10 classes at 28% fill, while the studio average was 45.4%.
Capacity is only wasted relative to demand. A short class in a small room can fill without changing who books it.
Check the seat count against the book, class by class
Programming
4,606 seats were offered for 2,090 attendances, so 2,516 seats went unsold.
Half the capacity problem is created by the room a class is put in. The seat count is editable and it costs nothing to change.
Decide the fate of every class that ran to nobody
Programming
4 classes had no attendees at all against 39 with two or fewer.
These are individual decisions, not a category. A one-page list with a keep, move or drop box next to each one clears the question in a single meeting.
Publish capacity, bookings and show rate for the coming week
Studio Manager
Utilisation for the month closed at 45.4%.
Seats sold three days ahead is a leading measure and it is available before the class runs. Show rate at the door is a lagging one.

chapters.title: Instructor Performance
facts: 14 trainers taught 328 classes and filled 2,090 seats for ₹19,01,973 in September 2026.
Utilisation spread 2.2 times, but revenue per attendee only 1.4 times - most of the gap is the slot.
4 classes ran to nobody; 10.1% of their booked seats were late-cancelled.
chapters.subtitle: 14 trainers, 2.2 times utilisation spread
recs_extra: Give Raunak Khemuka the slots that already work
Studio Manager
Raunak Khemuka fills 28.4% of 19 classes, the lowest on the roster, at ₹975 of revenue per attendee.
Re-timing rather than removing is the change: the same hands in a better hour usually closes half the gap without a single class being cut.
Pay for attendance, not for the size of the room
Studio Manager + Finance
Anmol Sharma delivers ₹1,076 of class revenue per attendee against a roster average of ₹910. Cost per attendance, not per class, is what decides whether an hour was worth having.
A rate anchored to attendance aligns the trainer, the timetable and the P&L on the same number and ends the incentive to fill a big room badly.
Assign first classes deliberately, by conversion
Programming + Sales
Conversion from a first class ranges from 0% to 41% across 3,337 recorded first classes.
This is the cheapest conversion growth available: no new leads, no price change, only a decision about who stands in front of a newcomer.
Stop separating trainer assessment from the ledger
Studio Manager
The payroll scorecard rates trainers on conversion and retention over a cycle; this chapter measures what they actually delivered, class by class. The two currently do not inform each other.
One page a month that shows both, side by side, turns an opinion about a trainer into an argument with evidence.
Review the slots nobody attended, with the trainer in the room
Programming
4 classes ran to nobody, and 3 trainers carry at least one of them.
An empty class is usually an hour rather than a person; the review should decide which one it found before anyone is reassigned.
chapters.summary: 14 trainers taught 328 classes in September 2026, drawing 2,090 attendances and ₹19,01,973 of revenue. Utilisation ranged from 28.4% to 61.6%, a 2.2-fold spread. But revenue per attendee ran only ₹769 to ₹1,076, so most of the spread is the slots rather than the trainers.

Studio Manager
Revenue per attendee runs only ₹769 to ₹1,076, while utilisation runs 28.4% to 61.6%.

Give the strongest filler more of the week
Programming + Studio Manager
Anmol Sharma fills 61.6% across 14 classes.
Where a trainer repeatedly fills the room they were given, the next marginal slot should be theirs before it is anyone else’s.
Track who brings new members, not just who teaches
Studio Manager + CRM
New-member flow varies by trainer and is recorded in the check-in ledger, but it is not on any scorecard.
A trainer who attracts first visits is doing acquisition work. That deserves to be visible.
Watch late-cancellation rate by trainer as a coaching number
Studio Manager
Rates range from 4.1% to 14.3% on the same booking policy.
A high rate usually means a slot that has drifted out of the members’ week, which is a scheduling answer, not a compliance one.
Pair the strongest filler with the weakest slot before cutting it
Programming + Studio Manager
Anmol Sharma fills 61.6% and Raunak Khemuka fills 28.4% on the same timetable.
Trialling the best performer in the weakest slot separates a demand problem from a coaching one, and it costs four weeks.
Give every regular a named trainer
Studio Manager + CRM
14 trainers taught 328 classes for 2,090 attendances.
The trainer relationship is the most durable retention asset a studio has. It has to be visible in the roster to be managed.
Review late-cancellation rate in the coaching conversation
Studio Manager
Rates run from 4.1% to 14.3% on one policy.
A rate that high is usually a slot that has slipped out of the members’ week. The fix is a timetable edit, not a reminder.
Cost the roster per attendance, not per class
Management + Finance
Revenue per attendance was ₹910 across the month.
Payroll per attendance is the only teaching cost that sits on the same basis as the revenue it supports.
Watch how many trainers share one format
Programming
Barre 57 holds 21% of all attendances and is taught by 11 different trainers.
Too many hands on one format flattens the standard and hides who is filling the room. The trainer list for each format belongs on the programming page.

chapters.title: Memberships Lapsed and Churned
facts: 11,710 memberships at this studio, 6,782 of them paid for, across ₹8,90,79,136 of recorded money.
42% of paid memberships survive thirty days and 1.9% survive a year.
The median paid membership lasts 27 days; 3,191 produced no attendance at all.
76,258,641 classes sit unspent on the book, worth about ₹7,62,58,641 of delivered value.
chapters.subtitle: 6,782 paid memberships, median life 27 days
recs_extra: Write the unspent classes back as visits, with a date on them
Front Desk + Finance
507 memberships used a quarter or less of what they bought, leaving 5,390 classes undelivered worth about ₹7,43,78,990.
Converting credit into booked attendance moves money the studio already holds onto the balance sheet and pulls the member back into a routine - the single cheapest retention action available.
Segment win-back by recency, not by lifetime value
CRM + Marketing
274 people were here in the last thirty days and still hold ₹1,26,27,533; the largest group, 1,290 people, has not been inside a year.
Contact cost per recovered member falls by an order of magnitude between those two groups, and the studio currently sends the same message to both.
Freeze, do not lose: treat a pause request as a save
Front Desk
1,458 memberships were frozen at some point and 12.1% are still live, against 3.6% of those that were never frozen.
A member who asks to pause is planning to return. Offering the pause before they offer the cancellation converts a churn event into a deferred one.
Put every member on a plan at the halfway point of their membership
Studio Manager
63% of measurable memberships attended less in their second half than their first, and 37% attended at least half as often. The change is visible before the status moves.
A mid-membership review - attendance so far, what is left, one specific class to book - is the only intervention in this chapter that can act before the lapse rather than after it.
chapters.summary: 11,710 memberships are in the Kwality House, Kemps Corner ledger, 6,782 of them paid. 42% of paid memberships survive thirty days and 5% survive six months. The median membership lasts 27 days and carries ₹13,135 of recorded cash. Single Class keeps its members best at 2% still live or renewed.

Members are not lost in a moment. They stop coming, and everything needed to see it is already recorded.

Run an activation sequence through the first fortnight
Front Desk + CRM
44% of paid memberships end within fourteen days and 58% within thirty.
The first two weeks decide the membership. A dated plan, a booked class and a call on day ten is the whole intervention.
Collect the unused classes
CRM + Front Desk
507 memberships used a quarter or less of what they bought, leaving 5,390 classes unspent.
Paid-for and undelivered is a liability and a warm reason to make contact.
Lead with the product that keeps its members
Sales + Marketing
Single Class is still live or renewed 2% of the time, the best rate in the range.
Renewal is a property of the product list before it is a property of the customer. What works should be sold first.
Put the churn number in the acquisition plan
Management + Finance
Median membership life is 27 days.
If most of the book has to be replaced each month, acquisition is a maintenance cost rather than a growth line, and it should be budgeted as one.
Make the mid-length products the default recommendation
Sales + Marketing
Memberships of 31 to 60 days carry ₹14,996 of average cash against ₹1,869 for a week-long product.
The short products are the ones that leave. What a member buys first predicts how long they stay far better than how much they liked the trial.
Convert the single-class buyers before the week is out
Front Desk + CRM
2,516 memberships lasted a week or less and used 0.44 classes each.
This is the largest, cheapest and most time-sensitive group in the ledger. A call on day three is worth more than any win-back offer in month three.
Work the not-activated and grace-period files monthly
CRM + Front Desk
324 memberships never activated and 329 sit inside the grace window.
Both are dated, small and contactable. A monthly standing list keeps this number from building up into a churn statistic.

CRM
507 memberships used a quarter or less of what they paid for, leaving 5,390 classes unspent.

Sales + Management
The median membership life is 27 days.
If the median life is inside the second month, a three-month product sets a different expectation and gives the studio two renewal conversations instead of one.

CRM
11,710 memberships sit in the ledger, 6,782 of them paid.
Members who joined in the same month behave similarly. Cohort lines show whether retention is improving or whether the mix is merely changing.

chapters.title: Format Comparisons
facts: 16 formats ran 328 classes for ₹19,01,973 in September 2026.
Strength Lab is the fullest at 86.0%; Recovery the emptiest at 15.0%.
Mat 57 earns the most per class at ₹10,360.
chapters.subtitle: 16 formats, 86% to 15% fill
recs_extra: Rebuild PowerCycle around what actually fills
Programming + Founder
PowerCycle holds 26% of the timetable and fills 48%. The best-filling format in the studio, Strength Lab, gets 11%.
Moving ten per cent of PowerCycle’s classes into the hours and rooms that already fill is worth roughly 3,173 attendances a month at current prices.
Market the second format to the devoted, not to everyone
Marketing + Front Desk
139 members made three or more visits to one format this month and 46% of members touched more than one format. Frequency concentrates in the members who already come.
One named class offered to a member in their fourth week of a single format is the highest-yield cross-sell the studio has, and it costs nothing but the message.
Try the empty day, once, before calling it unfillable
Programming
59 format-and-day combinations had no class at all this month. The studio has never tested them.
One four-week trial per gap, with the same trainer and hour as the successful version, turns an assumption into a fact at the cost of one slot.
chapters.summary: 16 formats ran 328 classes in September 2026 for ₹19,01,973. Strength Lab filled 86.0% of its seats against 15.0% for Recovery. Barre 57 reached the most members at 230.

Programming
Strength Lab runs 37 classes and fills 86.0% of them.

Sell the second format deliberately

46% of members used more than one format this month and 139 made three or more visits to a single one.

Programming + Studio Manager
Barre 57 holds 21% of all classes at 37.1% fill.
A single format holding a third of the week makes the studio’s utilisation a property of that format rather than of the timetable.
Move express formats into the peak hours
Programming
Mat 57 earns the most per class at ₹10,360 while the shortest formats run mostly off-peak.
The peak hour is the scarcest slot in the week and a short class is the cheapest way to use part of it.
Match the format to the room it is given
Studio Manager
Rooms fill from 39.6% to 59.4%, a gap driven by capacity rather than by demand.
Several formats can be run in more than one room. Moving the emptier ones into the smaller room raises utilisation without new members.
Retire or re-launch the formats under a real trial size
Programming
16 formats appear in the month, and the smallest ones ran only a handful of classes.
A format judged on five classes tells you nothing. Commit to a twelve-class trial or take it off the timetable and stop reporting it.
Watch the show rate of every format, not only the fill
Studio Manager
The month closed at 45.4% utilisation across 328 classes.
Formats that fill on paper but empty at the door behave differently from formats that convert bookings into attendance.

chapters.title: Late Cancellations and Discounts

kpis.label: Value at average
kpis.detail: opportunity cost, not a booked loss

facts: 234 seats were released late in September 2026, 10.1% of everything booked.
At ₹910 of revenue per attendance those seats are worth about ₹2,12,948.
1,265,715 rupees of discount went out on the same month, spread across 15% of transactions.
chapters.subtitle: 234 seats released late, 10.1% of the book
recs_extra: Send the reminder four hours out, not twenty-four
Front Desk + Systems
Late releases peak at 19:00 with 44 seats in September 2026. The decision to skip is made on the day, not the day before.
A reminder placed inside the decision window is the only nudge that can still change the outcome, and a waitlist text sent at the same moment converts the release into an attendance.
Talk to the members who cancel repeatedly, one at a time
Studio Manager
28 members cancelled three or more times this month and the ten most frequent produced 22% of all late releases.
A short call costs nothing, and for a member cancelling around a scheduling conflict it fixes the pattern in a way no rule about credits would.
Charge for the seat that cannot be resold, and refund the one that can
Founder + Finance
234 seats came back late at 10.1% of the book, and the release rate differs more by hour than by trainer.
A rule anchored to resale feasibility is fair enough that staff will enforce it, and it stops the studio taxing an 18:30 class to solve a 07:00 problem.
Cap the depth of the largest code and publish the ceiling
Marketing + Finance
PR1V@TE20 is 79% of all discounting in September 2026 at a mean depth of 70%.
One code at one depth is auditable. Four codes at four depths is a negotiation at the desk, and the desk always loses the argument it has to have twice a week.
Use the cancellation signal as an early warning, not a penalty
CRM + Studio Manager
Members with more than half their bookings cancelled are live 6% of the time against 3% for those who never cancel, on the whole membership ledger.
Reading a rising cancellation rate as an at-risk flag costs nothing and starts the retention conversation weeks before the lapse date.
chapters.summary: 234 seats were released late in September 2026, 10.1% of everything booked. That is down from 802 a year earlier. Attendance ran at 89.9% of the booked book, and the board is only 50.5% booked in the first place. Discount depth stands at 19.3% across 15% of sales.

Give the released seat back to the waitlist automatically
CRM + Front Desk
234 seats were released late, at an average board occupancy of 50.5%.
A seat released hours before the class is worth little to the studio and a great deal to a member who could not book.
Contact the members who cancel repeatedly
CRM
28 members cancelled three or more times, and the ten heaviest made 22% of all cancellations.
Repeat cancelling is a schedule that no longer fits. A short conversation is cheaper than a discount and more likely to hold them.
Set a discount ceiling and publish the range
Finance + Management
Depth across recent years runs from 8.4% to 19.3%.
Publishing the range, without naming anyone, moves behaviour faster than a policy does.
Test whether discounts buy loyalty at all
Marketing
Pooled comparisons flatter discounting because the products that carry offers are the ones that renew anyway.
A controlled test measured on renewal, not on units sold, would settle a question the studio has been answering by assumption.
Ask the members who never cancel for something
CRM + Marketing
4,445 members cancelled nothing this year and hold 3.1 live classes each.
This is the most committed list in the database and it is currently used for nothing. Reviews, referrals and price tests all start here.
Handle the heaviest cancellers as a scheduling problem
Studio Manager + CRM
387 members cancelled more than half their bookings and late-cancel 7.2% of the time.
That pattern describes a week that no longer fits. A short conversation about times is cheaper than a discount and more likely to hold them.
Check the timetable on the days that release most seats
Programming
Thursday released 45 seats late, Friday released 23.
Late releases cluster on particular days and hours. That is a timetable signal, not a member behaviour problem.
Re-price the seat that was released
Finance
234 seats were released late out of 2,325 booked.

Discount the quiet hour, not the product
Marketing + Finance
234 late releases against an average board occupancy of 50.5%.

chapters.title: Studio Overview and Intelligence
facts: 328 classes, 45.4% utilisation and ₹19,01,973 of delivered revenue in September 2026, against ₹32,06,431 of cash taken.
474 people trained here at 4.41 visits each.
147 members came in both September 2025 and September 2026; they came 140 fewer times this year, worth about ₹1,27,405 of delivered revenue.
1,068 leads sit open with a mean age of 782 days - unsold demand larger than the studio can serve in a year.
chapters.subtitle: 328 classes at 45.4%, ₹32,06,431 banked
recs_extra: Put a target on the open file and a date on every entry
Sales + Founder
1,068 leads are open, 46 of them arrived in the last thirty days and 984 are more than six months old.
The fresh block converts at a real rate and costs one conversation; the stale block costs a decision to close it. Both are cheaper than new leads.
Use the other 3 studios as the control group
Founder
This studio ranks 1 of 4 on utilisation in September 2026 (45.4% against a group median of 40.6%).
Any month where the studio moves with the group is a market month; any month where it moves alone is a decision. That distinction saves the studio from reacting to weather.
Publish these four numbers on one page, monthly
Studio Manager

Leads, trials, bookings against capacity and visits per member all move before the figures the studio currently watches. In September 2026 they read 189 new leads, 2,325 booked seats and 4.41 visits per member.
A leading indicator nobody publishes is a leading indicator nobody changes.

Management

Report four leading indicators monthly and nothing else
Management

Each can be read within a week of the month ending, and each predicts the others. One page would give the studio a month of warning.
Treat the live book as pipeline, not administration
CRM + Front Desk
6,782 paid memberships are on file and the warmest lapsed group is contactable today.
A dated, owned call list built from the studio’s own ledger is the highest-yield piece of work available.
Keep the gains on the record
Studio Manager
Revenue per class is ₹5,799 against ₹4,605 a year earlier.
Naming what improved protects it. A studio that only reports problems tends to lose the things that were working.
Report visits per member as the studio’s headline number
Management
474 members made 2,090 visits, 4.41 each, against 4.41 a year earlier.
It moves before revenue, before member counts and before payroll. Every other number on the page is downstream of it.
Put paying members and visiting members on the same page
Management + CRM
6,782 paid memberships are on the ledger and 474 members visited this month.
The gap between the two is the studio’s contactable pipeline. It should be worked as a list rather than reported as a ratio.
Set next month’s capacity plan from utilisation and not from last year’s revenue
Studio Manager
Utilisation was 45.4% on 328 classes and 4,606 seats.
Seats and hours are what the studio actually sells. Revenue follows the rooms, and the rooms are set a month ahead.
Protect the hours that already work
Programming
Tuesday fills 49.3% and 10:00 fills 49.6%.
Growth decisions are easy when the strongest blocks are named. It also stops a good slot being traded away for a quiet one.
Give the team one page a month and four numbers on it
Management
Leads, trials, bookings against capacity and visits per member all move before revenue does.
Each can be read within a week of the month ending. A single page is more likely to be acted on than a full review.

chapters.title: Lead Performance and Insights
facts: 5,709 leads on file for this studio: 1,991 trialled, 1,003 won, 888 retained.
Trials convert at 36.0% against those without one.
49% of wins closed on the day of the enquiry; 1,068 leads sit open with a mean age of 782 days.
chapters.subtitle: 5,709 leads, 34.9% trialled, 17.6% won
recs_extra: Make the trial the only acquisition target
Sales + Studio Manager
Leads who completed a trial convert at 36.0% and those who did not at 7.7%. On this file that is 1,991 leads sitting on the wrong side of a diary entry.
Every lead conversation ends with a time and a class, not a callback. At the studio’s current trial-to-win rate, a hundred more trials is worth roughly 28 more members a year.
Move acquisition effort toward Incoming sms and Client Referral
Marketing + Founder
Incoming sms converts at 40.9% with a mean LTV of ₹23,148 on 22 leads; the largest source, Website, converts at 7.0% on 1,446.
Tripling the smaller, better source costs less than the studio currently spends to fill the larger one and delivers members who stay longer.
Publish conversion by associate, with book size beside it
Studio Manager
Conversion runs 8.0% to 39.3% across books of 28 to 2217 leads.
Putting the two columns together on one page every month ends the argument about whose leads are worse and starts the one about what each person does with theirs.
Report leads weekly, on the stage they are stuck at
Founder + Sales
1,141 leads were contacted at most once, and the file shows follow-ups spanning a median of 7 days for decisions that usually take one.
A weekly thirty-minute review of the stuck stages is the only cadence that matches how quickly a lead goes cold.

Answer every enquiry the same day
Front Desk + CRM
49% of memberships are sold on the day of the enquiry.
Response time is the conversion rate, delayed. It is also the one variable in lead handling the studio controls completely.
Move acquisition towards the channels that convert
Marketing
Referrals & Word-of-Mouth converts 34.7% of its leads; Website & Online Sources converts 9.5%.
The studio does not need more leads, it needs the leads that already know someone. A published phone number and a referral reward are the cheapest mix changes available.
Close the open file honestly
CRM
1,068 leads are open at a mean age of 782 days, 984 of them older than six months.
A single pass to contactable, interested or closed turns thousands of rows into a short real list and makes every conversion figure trustworthy.
Move a share of acquisition spend towards referrals
Marketing
Referrals convert 38.3% of their leads at ₹8,639 of lifetime value; the website converts 7.0% at ₹2,646.
The cheapest mix change available is asking members who already refer well to do it more often. It needs a process, not a budget.
Put a named owner on the largest source
Front Desk + CRM
Website supplies 1,446 leads and converts 7.0%, the weakest rate of any large channel.
The largest pool is not the best one. Improving the biggest channel by two points is worth more than opening a new one.
Score associates on trials booked, not on leads held
Studio Manager
Associate conversion runs from 8.0% to 39.3% on comparable lead volumes.
Trials are the step the studio controls. Leads are demand; trials are work.
Work the open file from the freshest stage backwards
CRM
832 leads sit at the pricing stage and 125 at first contact.
Pricing-stage leads have already shown interest and need a decision, not a reminder sequence. They are the highest-yield calls on the list.
Match the enquiry to the class the lead asked about
Front Desk
Barre 57 converts 17.6% against 17.6% for the next best group.
Where a lead names a class, the trial booking should be that class. It is the cheapest personalisation available and it needs no system.

chapters.title: Member Behaviour and Patterns
facts: 474 members made 2,090 visits in September 2026 at 4.41 each; 214 came exactly once.
The median gap between visits across the studio’s whole ledger is 2 days and 87% of gaps are a week or less.
The tenth of the base that comes most produces 39% of all attendance.
Of 3,344 recorded first-timers, 22% reached a third visit - the point at which a 2-for-1 intro pack member is genuinely returning.
chapters.subtitle: 474 members, 4.41 visits each, 39% of attendance in the top tenth
recs_extra: Give the 214 once-only members a dated plan, not a reminder
Front Desk + Studio Manager
214 of the 474 members who attended in September 2026 came exactly once, 45% of the base. They are not a churn statistic; they are the next month’s frequency problem.

One booked class with a time attached, offered before the member leaves the building, converts a visit into a habit. On this month’s numbers a tenth of that group attending twice more is 43 extra attendances.
Build the at-risk list from the member’s own gap, not from the studio’s
CRM

The studio-wide median gap between visits is 2 days, but the distribution runs from one day later to a tail beyond two months. A fixed thirty-day rule flags half the base and misses the members who always came weekly and have just stopped.
A gap that stretches past a member’s own median is the earliest reliable warning the data contains, and it is computable from the ledger the studio already exports each day.
Sell the next purchase 11 days after the last
Front Desk + Finance
The median gap between purchases at this studio is 11 days and 66% of repeat purchases fall inside a month. Beyond that window the probability of a second purchase falls away.
A renewal conversation scheduled to the member’s own purchase rhythm rather than the expiry date is the difference between a renewal and a re-acquisition.
Program the middle of the day on purpose, not by residue
Programming
52 members take midday as their habit against 290 morning and 132 evening, and the midday group comes 1.00 times a month against 5.03 at the peak.
One format scheduled specifically for the middle of the day, with an off-peak price attached, converts idle mid-morning capacity rather than competing for the evening.
Count the third visit, not the second, as the return
Marketing + Founder

26% of recorded first-timers came back once after their trial but only 22% reached a third visit. A 2-for-1 pack member is a returning client on their third visit, and every retention measure built on the second one is flattering the studio.
Fixing the definition changes what the team optimises for, and costs nothing but a column in the report.
Protect the frequent tenth as a named group
Studio Manager
47 members produced 39% of all attendance in September 2026. A fifth of them changing habit moves the month more than any acquisition campaign on file.
A monthly watch-list, one message when someone in it stops coming, and no discount, is the cheapest revenue protection the studio has.
